---
title: "Books & Links"
---

## 📚 Textbooks
Books discussed below should be available in the UofT library in electronic form.

**For Introductory/General Reading:**
- N. Schroeghofer, *"Lessons in Scientific Computing"*, CRC 2019. (Focus on HPC languages vs Python).
- S. Linge, H. Langtangen, *"Programming for Computations - Python"*, Springer 2019.

**For Lectures L2+ (Fortran & Advanced Python):**
- J. Izaac and J. Wang, *"Computational Quantum Mechanics"*, Springer 2018.
- P. Turner, T. Arildsen, K. Kavanagh, *"Applied Scientific Computing with Python"*, Springer 2018.

## 🐧 Linux & Systems
You are encouraged to install Linux (Rocky, Red Hat, Ubuntu) or use MacOS (Unix-based) for this course.
- **CentOS / Rocky Linux:** Familiarize yourself with CLI (bash, tcsh) and SSH tools like PuTTY.
- [Linux Information Project](http://www.linfo.org/) - Explanations of commands, "bit", "byte", and history.
- [Bash Programming Intro HOWTO](http://tldp.org/HOWTO/Bash-Prog-Intro-HOWTO.html#toc7)

## 🌐 Networking & Parallel Computing
- **OpenMP:** Look up the "Hands-on intro to OpenMP" (SC08).
- **CUDA:** 
  - CUDA C Programming Guide (Nvidia).
  - CUFFT library description for Fast Fourier Transforms on GPU.
- **MPI:** For node-to-node communication (not explicitly required, but good to know).

## 📜 History
- History of computing, Alan Turing, Marian Rejewski, and the decoding of the ENIGMA machine during WWII.
- The evolution of supercomputers (e.g. Fugaku exaflop computing).
